meta.methodology: When a dated G2 rating is on file: value_score (0-100) = round(0.5 x fit + 0.3 x cost_score + 0.2 x sentiment_score). fit = editorial fit_score (1-5) x 20. cost_score = 100 - 60 x (entry_price - lowest entry price in the use case) / (highest - lowest); contact-sales tools get no cost or value score. sentiment_score = round(clip((Bayesian average - 3.0) / 2.0 x 100, 0, 100)), where Bayesian average = (50 x 4.3 + review_count x G2 rating) / (50 + review_count). Tools without review data are labeled "no review data yet" and keep value_score = round(0.625 x fit + 0.375 x cost_score). The category-wide value score uses the overall G2 rating. When segment ratings exist later, stack pages prefer the rating for that team size (solo/small -> small business, early/scaling -> mid-market, large -> enterprise). Stack picks also weigh fit for the GTM team size (reviewer company-size mix, case studies, enterprise-readiness evidence).
meta.disclaimer: Profitable Agent Stack is for general information only, provided "as is" without warranties. Prices, plans, features and review data change often and may be inaccurate or out of date (last checked 2026-11-23); always verify with the vendor. Cost estimates and scores are editorial estimates, not advice. Nothing here is professional, legal or financial advice. Trademarks belong to their owners; listing is not endorsement. Some links may be affiliate or sponsored — see our Disclosure.

data.name: Solo founder
data.who: One person doing all of go-to-market: you are the founder, the seller and the marketer. Your goal is the first repeatable customers, not a machine.
data.assumptions: 1 GTM person, 1 LinkedIn account, light volume. Hunter's free plan (50 credits/mo) caps how many new emails you can find; move up when you outgrow it. Monthly billing, entry tiers; Carrd is priced yearly ÷ 12.

items.reason: Highest value score for list building (free, fit 5/5). Exa is a free alternative if you prefer search-style prospecting. Free-plan limits change, so check them.
Free email finding and verification is enough for light hand-built lists.
Lowest published entry price for outbound email in our list. Instantly scores higher on value (93 vs 84) but costs $8 more; revisit at 2–5 people.
Cheapest listed LinkedIn tool and the best value score in its category. Per user, billed in euros.
Cheapest custom-domain landing page in our list; $19/yr is the yearly price on its Pro page.
Highest value score; free until you monetize. Kit is the free alternative (free up to 10,000 subscribers).
Free and good enough for basic traffic and source tracking at this size.

notes.title: Warm network & referrals
notes.text: Spreadsheet or notes app you already own. Message everyone you know who fits your ICP first; no tool is needed to do this.

notes.title: ICP & positioning
notes.text: Customer conversations plus a one-page doc. We list no paid tool for this job: talk to buyers first.

skip_for_now.use_case: Signals & intent data (RB2B, PostHog, Common Room)
skip_for_now.reason: Paid intent and visitor-identification tools tell you who to talk to. Until hand-built outbound gets replies, you have nobody to prioritize.
These are contact-sales products. An agent cannot fix messaging that does not work by hand yet.

skip_for_now.use_case: Social scheduling, search and content tools, design/video, community
skip_for_now.reason: Useful later; none of them is needed to get the first customers. Free Search Console is worth setting up when you publish.
No AI-search demand to measure yet, and warm leads and outbound come first. Revisit when content gets traffic.

crm.pick_tier: Google Sheet first, then HubSpot Free CRM (up to 2 users) when a signal below appears
crm.why: HubSpot Sales Hub has the largest small-business reviewer base among the CRMs we checked (60.5% of its G2 reviewers are small businesses) and native integrations with Apollo, Hunter, Smartlead and Waalaxy. Attio suits founders who want a flexible data model.
crm.spreadsheet_or_crm: A sheet is usually enough while you are the only person selling, live deals stay under about 20 and most come from your network. Move to a free CRM the week you turn on a sequencer, or once a follow-up slips.
crm.also: Zoho CRM Free (3 users), Bigin by Zoho Free (1 user) and Close Solo ($9/mo billed annually, built-in calling) also fit here.
crm.note: CRM is a separate category and is not included in stack totals.

data.assumptions: 3 GTM people, 2 LinkedIn users, ~5,000 emails/mo, monthly billing, entry tiers. Waalaxy is priced per user in euros and not converted.

items.reason: Highest value score for list building; free. Check current free-plan limits.
Hunter shares one credit pool across unlimited team members (vendor help center), so adding people does not add seats.
Highest value score for outbound (93). Unlimited mailboxes on one plan; its lead credits are not added because Hunter covers enrichment.
Light LinkedIn volume at the lowest per-user price. Move to HeyReach when you run many senders.
Free first-party search data. Paid content optimization waits until you publish weekly.

Free for up to 3 channels. Typefully is a free alternative and currently has the higher value score (88 vs Buffer 83) because Buffer's verified G2 rating is in the score and Typefully has no review data yet.
Multi-page site with your own domain for content/SEO. Carrd is cheaper but single-page.
Free until you monetize.
Free web analytics; add product/funnel analytics later.
Optional, and only if warm intros plus outbound are already booking meetings: free website-visitor identification to prioritize follow-up.

notes.text: Revisit with real call notes; no paid tool listed for this job.

Contact-sales pricing and little to feed it yet.
Use Search Console and publish first; add paid content tools once content is a weekly habit.

crm.pick_tier: Free if 2 people work deals; Starter for 3 (3 seats × $20 list)
crm.why: HubSpot integrates natively with Instantly, Hunter, Apollo and Waalaxy, so replies and meetings can log themselves. HubSpot currently shows a limited-time lower Starter price for new customers; we use list price. Pipedrive is a strong choice for a simple visual pipeline (75.1% of its G2 reviewers are small businesses).
crm.spreadsheet_or_crm: A shared sheet can work for a short while, but at 2–5 a second person usually already works the pipeline, which is the clearest signal to add a CRM.
crm.also: Attio and Zoho CRM are free for up to 3 users. Close Essentials ($35/user/mo billed annually) fits phone-heavy teams.

data.name: Early scaling

data.assumptions: 10 GTM people, 5 LinkedIn senders, ~25,000 emails/mo (inside Instantly's 125,000/mo Hypergrowth tier), monthly billing. Surfer is its yearly-billed view; Framer is its yearly-billing view. PostHog counted at its free allowance (usage-based beyond it). Peec AI is its Starter monthly list price.

items.reason: Free is for 'exploring or very light usage' per Apollo; we count $0 for light list pulls, but 6-15 people will likely outgrow it. Basic is $49/seat/mo billed annually (not counted). 28% of Apollo's 9,858 G2 reviewers are mid-market (51-1,000 employees).
Clearer enrichment: more credits shared across unlimited team members, and verification before sending.
Full outbound volume on one plan; highest value score for outbound.
Built for many senders (fit 5/5). Waalaxy is cheaper per seat if you only need light LinkedIn volume.
Signals become useful at this volume: identifies site visitors to feed outbound.
Free first-party data on which queries bring visitors (search performance).
Content optimization is a separate job from search performance tracking. Discovery is its lowest listed tier.

Lowest-priced dedicated AI-search tracker with a published price we found that fits a team: 50 prompts on 3 models, unlimited users, SOC 2 on every plan. Surfer is not the AEO pick: its AI tracker is an add-on to content editing, and this is a different job. Start small; skip if AI search is not yet a channel.
Team scheduling beyond Buffer's free 3-channel limit.
Design-led site with custom domain; lowest paid tier.
Free until you monetize (Lite is $49/mo, yearly-billing view).
Website traffic and sources.

data.name: Scaling
data.who: Sixteen to forty people in go-to-market, several managers, and RevOps starting to own reports, permissions and data hygiene.
data.assumptions: 25 GTM people, 10 LinkedIn senders, high email volume (125,000/mo), monthly list prices except Apollo (10 prospecting seats, billed annually); Webflow and Surfer are yearly-billed views. RB2B Pro is a 'from' price. PostHog counted at its free allowance (usage-based beyond it). Peec AI is its Pro monthly list price.

items.reason: Free is for 'exploring or very light usage' per Apollo, so we count Basic for the 10 people who prospect ($49/seat/mo billed annually, credits pooled across the team). 28% of Apollo's 9,858 G2 reviewers are mid-market (51-1,000 employees), roughly 2,800 reviewers. Professional ($79) adds waterfall enrichment, which overlaps Hunter, so it is not counted. Confirm seats and credits with the vendor.

Largest listed tier; unlimited team members share one credit pool, so no per-seat cost. G2 shows 31.9% of Hunter's 659 reviewers are mid-market (about 210) versus 24.8% of Clay's 234 (about 58), so Clay is not clearly the mid-market pick. Step up to Clay Growth ($495/mo monthly list) when RevOps needs CRM auto-sync, phone numbers and signals; the Large stack uses Clay.
Cost-first pick at this volume. Test its admin and role controls in the trial; Reply.io, Salesloft or Outreach are the step-ups when you need org-level roles and a sales-engagement suite (see Large).
Multi-seat: its help center documents Admin and Member roles with per-feature permissions.
Signals are core at this size. RB2B Pro is the lowest-cost listed paid tier; Common Room ($2,500/mo) is the step-up for community and multi-channel signals.
Free first-party search performance data.
Content optimization, a separate job from search performance.

150 prompts, 3 countries and 2 projects, plus API access for reporting. Dedicated AEO tracker with published pricing; AthenaHQ ($295) and Scrunch ($250) are the alternatives, Profound is contact sales.
Social scheduling across a marketing team.
CMS-capable site for a content team; lowest CMS tier on its pricing page.
Free until you monetize; Pro is $95/mo (yearly-billing view).
Website traffic and sources.
Queryable product/funnel analytics. Pipeline and revenue reporting belong in your CRM, which this directory does not cover.

crm.pick_tier: Professional, 25 seats × $90 billed annually, plus $1,500 one-time onboarding
crm.why: Professional adds forecasting and advanced automation. data.name: Large / multi-team
data.who: More than forty people across several teams or regions. Procurement, security review and data-processing agreements are part of buying anything.
data.assumptions: 40+ GTM people across teams, 25 of them prospecting in Apollo (Organization, billed annually, 3-seat minimum), ~25 LinkedIn senders (HeyReach Agency tier), monthly list prices except Apollo and Common Room (billed annually, Common Room 5 seats). Clay is its Growth monthly list price; its Enterprise tier is custom. Salesloft (outbound) has no public price and counts as $0 here; expect a per-seat, annual quote with a seat minimum. Peec AI is Advanced's monthly list price; SSO needs its Enterprise quote. Enterprise tiers, SSO and security documents are quote-based. This total is a floor, not a quote.

items.reason: Not the free Starter: 40+ people need SSO and admin controls, which Apollo sells on Organization ($119/seat/mo billed annually) and its Custom plan. Size evidence: of 9,858 G2 reviews, 28% come from mid-market and 5% from enterprise companies (roughly 2,800 and 450 reviewers), Apollo publishes a 130-rep customer story (Superside), and it lists SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in its trust center. Seats assumed: 25 of your 40+ people prospect. ZoomInfo has a larger enterprise review share (26%) but no public price: quote both.

Clay's Enterprise tier lists SSO/SAML, SCIM, role-based access, IP allowlists and a custom DPA, it states SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, and its case studies include Intercom, Verkada and Rippling. Hunter's public pages list a custom enterprise volume plan but no SSO. Caveat: Clay's G2 reviewers skew small (74% under 51 employees, 1% enterprise), with a learning curve and fast credit use as top complaints, so pilot with credit budgets. $495 is Growth's monthly list price; SSO and RBAC need the Enterprise quote.

items.tier: Enterprise quote (per seat, no public list price)
items.reason: Pick over Outreach for a 40+ team: G2 reviewers are 32.6% enterprise and 50.9% mid-market (4,287 reviews) versus 21.7% and 59.2% for Outreach (3,574), G2 rates its ease of setup 8.6 vs 7.7 and support 8.6 vs 8.3, and it publicly documents SAML SSO (Okta, Entra, OneLogin) plus SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 with a public trust portal. No public price: $0 is counted, so this total is a floor. Outreach is the close alternative (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 42001; trust center only via an account exec). Salesloft merged with Clari (Dec 2025): ask about packaging and renewal terms.
$999/mo for 25 senders beats $79 × 25. Roles are documented, but we found no SOC 2 claim and its DPA says SSO is not currently supported: confirm with security.
Vendor security page lists a SOC 2 Type 2 report, GDPR and CCPA, SSO/SAML/SCIM and role-based access.
Free first-party search performance data.
Content optimization, a separate job from search performance; check seat limits for multiple teams.

items.tier: Advanced, monthly list (SSO needs Enterprise quote)
items.reason: Advanced lists 350 prompts, 5 projects and a Data Studio connector, and SOC 2 is on every plan, but SSO is Enterprise-only (custom price): get a quote if security requires SSO. Profound (contact sales; SOC 2, SSO/SAML) is the enterprise-first alternative, and AthenaHQ and Scrunch also list Enterprise SSO. We found no G2 reviewer-size data for these tools.
Social scheduling across teams.
